whatIs: This is Project Wallace's CSS quality tool: it analyzes your CSS and gives it a score from 0 to 100 for performance, maintainability and complexity, with recommendations to improve each area.
You can give it a site's URL, upload CSS files or paste the code. It's a good fit when you want a quick assessment; for more detailed metrics, the same site has a full CSS analyzer.
uses: Getting a quick diagnosis of the CSS of an already published site from its URL.
Reviewing a pasted stylesheet before bringing it into a project.
Seeing whether your CSS is weaker in performance, maintainability or complexity to decide what to tackle first.
caveats: It's an assessment based on the tool's own criteria, so the score is a guide, not a standard.
Turning on the option to format the CSS makes it easier to read but slightly changes the numbers.
It only gives scores and general recommendations; to see metrics like specificity or selector complexity you have to go to the site's CSS Analyzer.
pricingNote: Free to use, with no sign-up or payment.
idealFor: Getting a quick score for the quality of your CSS.
